1. THE BLENDED INDEX IS ONLY VISIBLE THROUGH ITS SYMPTOM, AND THE SYMPTOM IS OPTIONAL. check_forecast_anchor fires on a declining MARGIN RATE. Apply one cumulative index to fuel, transport and overhead AND escalate the price path on the same index and the margin is FLAT by construction — nothing fires, while the decomposition still buys nothing and a real divergence between imported fuel and domestic wages is invisible. The value error arrives entirely through the level of the cost stack, not through its slope.

2. THE GATE IS ONE-SIDED BY DESIGN. Its own docstring records ARCC's rising path: "A gate that only catches declines would have said nothing here either, so the record is printed for every study whether or not it fires." Where it does fire, a study clears it by declaring 'input_cost_outpacing_price' with a disclosure and a period pair in which cost per unit of revenue rose — routine in an inflating economy. gaps.residual_gap:
The mode is uncovered as stated. One indirect, magnitude-only partial catch narrows it and must be stated honestly:

check_valuation_gap.py (GAP_LIMIT = -0.10 / GAP_LIMIT_ABOVE = +0.10) reads the committed central against the committed spot, both in the listing currency. A dropped peg puts the central at 1.53 against a spot of 6.16, a -75% gap, so R-GAP-01 would demand a GAP_REVIEW and R-GAP-02's publish block would hold the study. Its AUDITED CENTRAL marker would also go red against the existing review (ADNOCLS currently reads "-18.2% GAP_REVIEW_04-09-2026.md (audits 5.6100)"), so a moved central cannot ride the old review.

Four residual holes remain inside that partial catch:
(1) It is currency-blind and content-blind. The release is an AUTHORED eight-heading review whose headings are coverage-checked, not correctness-checked. An analyst who genuinely believes the USD figure writes a review auditing 1.5263 and the gate goes green.
(2) It is ONE-SIDED for the block. Applying the conversion TWICE puts the central 3.67x too HIGH (20.58 against 6.16, +234%). Per [R-GAP-02 AMENDED] the hold fires only where the central is BELOW price, so that direction ships with only an authored audit owed.
(3) The gap ratchet (gap_outstanding.json) permits listed studies to fail, so on a ratcheted name the currency error is invisible.
(4) It fires on MAGNITUDE, not on the relationship. It gives no coverage at all to the general form of the mode — a per-share output whose unit is unstated — and would say nothing about, e.g., an AED-listed study mistakenly using the SAR 3.75 peg (2.1%, below the materiality bar but the same defect class), nor about which of the two sides the factor was applied to.

The specific uncovered assertion: nothing requires bridge_record to declare the currency its per_share is in, and nothing reconciles per_share x declared fx to the published central. A gate closing it must accept BOTH committed spellings (`currency` and `reporting_currency`) — the book uses `currency` in 14 studies and `reporting_currency` in 2, which is exactly the L-355 trap that would make a naive gate silently exempt ADNOCLS and ADNOCDRILL, the two USD names that matter most.

gaps.name: The multiple the fair value implies contradicts the multiple the same study calls fair
gaps.mechanism: A study publishes a relative-multiple cross-check at a multiple it justifies from peers or its own history (say 9.0x), and a cash-flow central that, divided into the same metric on the same share count and net debt, asserts a completely different multiple (19.15x). Both numbers are correct arithmetic and individually defensible; the disagreement lives BETWEEN them, so no per-figure or per-lens check can see it. The analyst never performs the division because the model runs the other way — drivers to value — and the multiple is only ever computed on the price, never on the answer.

gaps.name: A published branch or bear leg sits below the company's own net cash per share
gaps.mechanism: A DCF bear scenario flexes an operating driver to its worst filed level and the operating present value collapses toward zero; the bridge then adds net cash, but if the bear is produced by flexing the equity value rather than the enterprise value — or if the cash is bridged at the base case only — the published per-share bear can fall beneath cash the company already holds. That is an arithmetic impossibility short of the cash being trapped or consumed, and nothing asserts the floor. The bear leg is what a reader takes as the downside, and it is exactly the number nobody audits because the gap gate reads only the central.
